claims.text: The as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloy has a single-phase hexagonal structure.
The as-deposited alloy contains significant microstructural heterogeneity, including variable grain boundaries and internal stresses.
Rapid deposition methods produce the stated microstructural heterogeneity in this alloy.
Annealing at 0.5–0.8 T_m under an inert atmosphere can relieve internal stress and make the microstructure more uniform without forming secondary phases.
Within the selected single-phase annealing window, annealing predominantly changes ordering and relaxes internal strain.
Annealing decreases internal strain and makes the grain-boundary distribution more uniform.
Reduced strain and a more uniform grain-boundary distribution produce more homogeneous exchange interactions.
More homogeneous exchange interactions synchronize the onset or nucleation of the magnetostructural transition throughout the sample.
Synchronizing the magnetostructural transition broadens its temperature window and makes its changes less abrupt.
A broader, less abrupt transition reduces hysteresis losses while maintaining an efficient magnetocaloric effect.
Compared with the as-deposited material, the annealed material will exhibit a wider temperature range of magnetic entropy change under fields below 1 T.
Annealing will reduce hysteresis, as indicated by lower coercivity and reduced hysteresis energy loss.
Transition broadening will cause a modest decrease in the maximum magnetic entropy change.
The combination of transition broadening, reduced hysteresis, and a modestly lower entropy-change peak will improve overall refrigerant capacity at low applied fields.
The as-deposited alloy has a sharp, hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transition with a large peak magnetic entropy change.
Microstructural heterogeneity in the as-deposited alloy limits heat-exchange efficiency and increases hysteresis losses.
The predictions apply only while the annealed alloy retains its single-phase hexagonal structure and avoids grain coarsening and secondary-phase formation.
Failure to obtain both a statistically significant hysteresis reduction and a broadened magnetocaloric response relative to an untreated control would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says homogenization synchronizes transition onset throughout the sample, but then predicts that this synchronization broadens the transition. Synchronization would ordinarily imply a narrower distribution of local transition temperatures, so the stated mechanism does not coherently produce the predicted broadening.

Secondary-phase formation is excluded from the domain in which the predictions are said to hold, yet it is also listed as a result that falsifies the mechanism. An out-of-bound processing result should invalidate the test conditions rather than decisively falsify the in-domain mechanism.
